spatial_claims.claim: D is the midpoint of segment BC, so BD = BC/2
E is a point on segment AB such that AE * EB = sq(BD), placed by 6.28
Semicircle AGB is described on AB as diameter; G lies on the semicircle
EG is perpendicular to AB, meeting the semicircle at G
Angle AGB is a right angle (G on semicircle with diameter AB)
GE is the altitude from the right-angle vertex G to hypotenuse AB, creating similar triangles AGE, GBE, AGB via 6.8
AE + EB = AB (E lies between A and B on segment AB)
AG/GE = AB/GB from similarity correspondence AGE ~ AGB, giving AG*GB = GE*AB

configuration_map: E is on segment AB, strictly between A and B (AE*EB > 0). G is on the semicircle with diameter AB, located where the perpendicular from E meets the semicircle. GE is the altitude from the right-angle vertex G to the hypotenuse AB in right triangle AGB. This creates the standard configuration for 6.8: two sub-triangles AGE and GBE, each similar to the whole triangle AGB. E serves consistently as both the point from 6.28 application and the foot of the altitude from G. G serves consistently as a point on the semicircle (giving the right angle at G) and the vertex from which the altitude is drawn.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction (semicircle on diameter AB, perpendicular from E meeting semicircle at G, similar triangles from altitude to hypotenuse) is a standard well-known configuration. E is consistently between A and B; G is consistently on the semicircle with EG perpendicular to AB; the right angle at G and the similar triangle decomposition via 6.8 are all compatible. No angle decomposition issues arise since no angle is written as a sum of parts. The proof is predominantly algebraic (commensurability arguments) with a standard geometric construction that introduces no spatial contradictions.
